# Playbook for ref_auction

## Budget Management
When I consider any bid, I must track my remaining budget accurately throughout the game. I should not rely on assumptions about my budget—I need to know exactly what I have left after each winning bid. I notice I stated conflicting budget figures in my record, which created confusion about my actual spending power.

## Valuation vs. Price Discipline
When a lot's value to me is below the estimate, I pass in round 1. Only in round 2, if the standing bid has dropped significantly below my valuation, do I reconsider entering.

When a lot's value to me is well above the standing bid, I enter the bidding immediately, even in round 1. The sooner I establish my interest, the better I can control escalation.

## Strategic Raising
When I decide to bid, I raise by the minimum required amount, not more. This preserves my budget for subsequent lots and keeps the price as low as possible while maintaining my position.

## Lot Prioritization
I assess all five lots mentally before the auction begins (if possible) to identify which ones offer me the most value. I prioritize competing hardest on lots where my private valuation is highest relative to the estimate.

## End-Game Awareness
When I reach the final lot, I remember that this is my last chance to win value. If I'm behind on score and the final lot has high personal value to me, I should be more aggressive than I was in earlier rounds, within the constraint of my remaining budget.

## What Did Not Work
Passing on Lot 1 when the round 2 bid was only 13, versus my valuation of 14, was too passive. I left potential gain on the table. In future, I should bid on narrow margins in final rounds, especially early in the auction when I have full budget.

# Playbook for Auction

When I'm shown a lot's value to me versus the estimate, I immediately compare them to identify whether this lot represents good value or poor value.

When the standing high bid is zero and I value the lot above the estimate, I open with a modest bid around 10% of the estimate to establish position without overcommitting.

When the standing high bid is already placed and I value the lot significantly above it (by more than 50%), I raise to win, calculating that even a minimum raise leaves me with substantial profit.

When the standing high bid is zero and I value the lot below the estimate, I pass immediately rather than opening bidding on a lot that's unlikely to be profitable.

When a lot's value to me is only marginally above the standing high bid (within 10-20%), I pass to preserve budget for future lots where I have clearer advantage.

When I'm in the final round of bidding on the last lot, I bid aggressively if the value proposition is positive, since there are no future lots to save budget for.

When calculating whether to raise, I always check that my bid leaves me with positive profit (value minus bid amount) before committing.

I track my spending across lots and never let any single lot consume so much budget that I cannot bid meaningfully on remaining lots.

I recognize that my earlier bidding mistakes (like bidding on lot 2 worth only 11 to me, or bidding on lot 5 worth 17 to me at minimum raise of 12 giving only 5 points profit) damaged my score. Going forward, I only bid on lots where my personal value exceeds the standing bid by at least 20-30% to ensure sufficient margin.

# Playbook for ref_auction

When I see a lot with high personal value relative to the current bid, I will bid aggressively in round 1 to secure it early, even if the minimum raise is modest.

When I'm in round 2 of a lot and the standing bid is still significantly below my valuation, I will raise to win rather than pass, since I've already committed to competing.

I will track my cumulative spending throughout the auction and ensure I have sufficient budget remaining to bid on high-value lots that appear late.

When deciding whether to bid, I will compare the standing bid plus minimum raise against my personal valuation. If winning at that price leaves me with positive surplus value, I will bid.

I will not be overly conservative with my budget early on if I encounter high-value lots. My final score was only +31, suggesting I left value on the table by being too cautious. I should bid more aggressively on lots worth substantially more than the current asking price.

I will bid in every round where a lot is worth significantly more to me than the standing bid, rather than passing and hoping the price stays low. The auction will move on without me if I don't participate.

I notice my budget tracking was inconsistent across bids—my stated remaining budget didn't always reflect what I had actually spent. Before my next game, I will develop a clear system for tracking cumulative expenditure so I know exactly what I can afford to bid.
